   MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  NORWALK COMMUNITY PROMOTION COMMISSION
  September 14, 2026

Chair Ang called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. and Vice Chair Lopez led the Flag Salute.
Responding to roll call were Chair Ang, Vice Chair Lopez, Commissioner Garcia, and Commissioner
Sanchez. Also present was Levy Sun, Director of Communications, Alex Ocegueda, Office Assistant
III, Marcus Dawal, Communications Specialist, Public Safety Commissioners Patricia Hoskins and
Richard LeGaspi.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Sanchez made the motion and Vice Chair Lopez seconded to approve the minutes for
August 10, 2026. There being no objection, the motion carried.

REPORTS

First Responders Luncheon

Mrs. Ocegueda presented the catering quotes received for the luncheon. After careful discussion and
consideration, the Commissioners selected Lupita’s Mexican Restaurant to cater the event. Public
Safety Commissioner LeGaspi confirmed that he secured a donation of eight cases of water from
Norwalk-La Mirada Plumbing Company. Commissioner LeGaspi also recommended inviting the
C.E.R.T program participants to volunteer at the event. Commissioner Sanchez requested that staff
photograph the students’ placemat artwork and prepare a thank-you letter recognizing the students for
their contributions. Mrs. Ocegueda reminded Commissioners to arrive at the event no later than 11:00
a.m. to assist with final preparations prior to the luncheon.

Holiday Décor Contest

Mrs. Ocegueda presented the new title, “Slay the Décor Holiday Competition,” along with two logo
options for the Commissioners’ consideration. After reviewing both designs, the Commissioners
unanimously agreed to move forward with Logo Option No. 1. Mrs. Ocegueda confirmed that the
Commission will have a booth at the upcoming Halloween Festival to promote the competition and
provide information to residents. She also confirmed that small giveaway bags featuring the new
competition logo will be ordered for distribution at the festival.

Commissioners Appreciation Dinner

Mrs. Ocegueda asked the Commissioners to continue their discussion regarding the voting criteria to
be established for the recognition certificates. Commissioners discussed the importance of finalizing
the criteria by February so that Mrs. Ocegueda can present the criteria to the Commission liaisons,
allowing the voting process to take place during their respective April meetings. After further discussion,
the matter was tabled for continued discussion at the next Commission meeting.
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Community Promotion Commission
September 14, 2026

Merchandise

Mr. Sun explained that the Commission would need to establish a program, like the previously
discussed Student Art Competition, to help launch the merchandising component the Commissioners
are interested in developing. He clarified that the proposed Student Art Competition itself would require
collaboration with the Art in Public Places Committee, as the competition would involve student artwork
and could potentially serve as the foundation for future merchandise featuring the students’ designs.
Mr. Sun proposed that the Commission meet with the Art in Public Places Committee to discuss the
concept, logistics, and potential structure of the Student Art Competition, as well as how the two
committees could collaborate on the program. The Commissioners agreed to meet with the Committee
to further discuss the proposal and determine the next steps. Mrs. Ocegueda confirmed that the Art in
Public Places Committee’s October meeting is scheduled for October 27.

Keepin’ It Norwalk

Mr. Sun presented the “Keepin’ It Norwalk” campaign video, August Family Fun Spots edition, to the
Commissioners.

Communications Analytics

Mr. Sun provided the analytics and explained Key Performance Indicators (KPI) and the city’s overall
reach across all outreach platforms for the last month showing an increase in key metrics.

STAFF COMMENTS:

Mr. Sun informed the Commission that Rosalee Santa Ana has submitted her resignation, and her last
day will be September 24, 2026.

COMMISSIONERS COMMENTS:

Vice Chair Lopez shared details of her interaction with school staff while picking up the placemats,
noting how enthusiastic and excited the students were to have been invited to contribute their artwork.
Commissioner Sanchez shared a similar experience when picking up the artwork, discussed attending
the 9/11 ceremony at John Glenn High School, and provided the latest updates on the Halloween
Parade. Chair Ang shared he attended a retirement party at Mr. Rosewoods and is looking forward to
starting his Route 66 road trip in his dune buggy.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

Resident Brian Tindell thanked the Commission for establishing the Native Plant Contest and brought
forward a suggestion related to the City’s Urban Forest Master Plan. Mr. Tindell expressed hope that
the Commission could assist in advancing the idea. He referenced information in the Master Plan
indicating that the City has an estimated deficit of approximately 10,000 trees and that, at the current
rate of planting, it could take approximately 25 years to reach the City’s tree-planting goals.
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Community Promotion Commission
September 14, 2026

Mr. Tindell suggested that the City consider opening a tree-planting program to interested residents,
allowing individuals to sponsor a tree and cover the associated planting costs. He recommended
promoting the program as an opportunity to plant a tree in dedication or honor of a child, family member,
or other individual. He also suggested that the City explore similar programs implemented by other
cities, such as the City of Oakland, as a potential model for developing the program.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:29 p.m.

_____________________________

David Ang, Chair
Community Promotion Commission
